items.followUp: Name two major biological issues faced by Pakistan.

rubric.why: Award for identifying two relevant biological issues.
rubric.how: Accept any two appropriate issues, such as food shortage, disease, energy crisis, environmental pollution or population growth.

rubric.why: A further valid issue earns the second mark if the first point was already awarded for another issue.
rubric.how: Award for a second distinct issue from the accepted examples.

modelAnswer: Major biological issues include food shortage, disease, energy crisis, environmental pollution and population growth.

items.followUp: State two contributions of Carolus Linnaeus to biology.

rubric.why: Linnaeus introduced the system of naming organisms with two names.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the two-part scientific naming system.

rubric.why: Linnaeus made an important contribution to the classification of organisms.
rubric.how: Award for stating that he developed or advanced the classification of organisms.

modelAnswer: Carolus Linnaeus introduced binomial nomenclature, in which each organism is given a two-word scientific name.
He also developed a systematic method for classifying organisms.

items.followUp: Why is the Houbara bustard considered an important bird in Pakistan?

rubric.why: The Houbara bustard is known as a migratory bird that visits Pakistan in winter.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it migrates to Pakistan, particularly in winter.

rubric.why: The bird is threatened by hunting and is a focus of conservation efforts.
rubric.description: Mentions its threatened status or conservation.
rubric.how: Award for noting that hunting threatens it or that it needs protection.

modelAnswer: The Houbara bustard is a migratory bird that comes to Pakistan in winter, usually from Central Asia.
It is endangered because of hunting and needs protection.

items.followUp: Give two differences between the primary and secondary cell walls.

rubric.why: The primary wall is formed first and is relatively thin and flexible.
rubric.description: States a feature of the primary cell wall.
rubric.how: Award for saying it forms first, is thin, or is flexible while the cell grows.

rubric.why: The secondary wall forms later and is generally thicker and more rigid, often containing lignin.
rubric.description: States a feature of the secondary cell wall.
rubric.how: Award for saying it forms after growth, is thick/rigid, or contains lignin.

modelAnswer: The primary cell wall is formed first while the cell is growing; it is thin and flexible.
The secondary cell wall is deposited inside the primary wall after cell growth; it is thicker and often strengthened with lignin.

items.followUp: What happens to a plant cell placed in a hypertonic solution?

rubric.why: A hypertonic solution has a higher solute concentration than the cell contents.
rubric.how: Award for comparing its solute concentration with that of the cell.

rubric.why: A hypotonic solution has a lower solute concentration, so water tends to enter the cell.
rubric.how: Award for the lower solute concentration or the resulting inward movement of water.

modelAnswer: A hypertonic solution has a higher solute concentration than the cell contents, so water moves out of the cell.
A hypotonic solution has a lower solute concentration than the cell contents, so water moves into the cell.

items.followUp: What is the difference between disjunction and non-disjunction during cell division?

rubric.why: Disjunction is the normal separation of chromosome pairs or chromatids during cell division.
rubric.how: Award for stating that chromosomes or chromatids separate and move apart.

rubric.why: Non-disjunction is a failure of chromosomes or chromatids to separate properly, producing cells with abnormal chromosome numbers.
rubric.how: Award for stating that separation fails or that chromosomes are distributed unequally.

modelAnswer: Disjunction is the normal separation of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to opposite poles during cell division.
Non-disjunction is the failure of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate properly, causing an abnormal chromosome number in the resulting cells.

items.followUp: What is the optimum pH of an enzyme?

rubric.why: The optimum temperature is the temperature at which an enzyme works at its highest rate.
rubric.how: Award for linking the temperature to maximum or fastest enzyme activity.

modelAnswer: The optimum temperature is the temperature at which an enzyme catalyses a reaction at its maximum rate.

items.followUp: What happens to enzyme activity when the pH moves away from its optimum?

rubric.why: Each enzyme has a particular pH at which it works best.
rubric.description: States that enzymes have an optimum pH.
rubric.how: Award for identifying a specific pH at which enzyme activity is greatest.

rubric.why: A pH different from the optimum reduces enzyme activity and can alter the enzyme's shape or active site.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of changing pH.
rubric.how: Award for reduced activity or an effect on enzyme structure/active site.

modelAnswer: Each enzyme has an optimum pH at which its activity is greatest.
A pH above or below this optimum reduces enzyme activity; a large change can alter the active site and denature the enzyme.
